finding.claim: The /rss endpoint passes the user-supplied `u` query parameter directly to URI.open with no validation. An attacker can make the server fetch internal or cloud-metadata URLs such as http://169.254.169.254/ or http://localhost:port/, and the first 400 bytes of the response are returned to them (non-blind SSRF). With open-uri, Kernel#open-style behavior may also apply on older Ruby versions, but URI.open itself already allows http, https and ftp.

trace.note: params[:u] is passed unvalidated to URI.open, which issues the server-side request
the first 400 bytes of the response body are returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No scheme check, no host allowlist, no private/link-local IP blocking, and no redirect restriction. The TRUSTED allowlist is only applied in /trusted, not in /rss.

verdict.reason: app.rb:8 passes the unauthenticated query param params[:u] straight into URI.open(...).read with no scheme or host validation (the TRUSTED allowlist at app.rb:14 only guards /trusted), and app.rb:9 returns the first 400 bytes to the caller.
